newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WIEBE LEADS KEMPER OPEN AFTER THREE ROUNDS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WIEBE LEADS KEMPER OPEN AFTER THREE ROUNDS.

text.p: Mark Wiebe, looking for his first PGA Tour victory since 1986, carded five birdies in a span of eight holes on Saturday to open a three-stroke lead after the third round of the Kemper Open.
Wiebe made all five of his birdies from outside 15 feet on his way to a six-under-par 66 in a demanding breeze at the Avenel TPC course.
At 11-under 202, Wiebe held the outright lead with one round left for the first time in his unspectacular career.
"I had a bunch of putts that went right in the middle. I had one of those days when I had the range from 25 feet," Wiebe said.

Mike Springer fired a 67 that left him alone in second place at eight-under 205 with three-time Masters champion Nick Faldo in third at 206 after carding a 68 in this final tune-up for next week's U.S. Open.
"I'm tickled to be in the lead, but I'm so busy thinking about what I have to do to hit the ball straight that I don't have time to think about anything else," admitted Wiebe.
The 39-year-old Wiebe has two career victories -- one in 1985 and one in 1986 -- but has not come close to winning since the 1993 Buick Classic, where he lost a playoff.
After a slow start to the season, Wiebe is on the upswing since recently being diagnosed as being allergic to several types of trees and grasses.
He is receiving two injections a week to control the problem, and they appear to be working: "I haven't been sneezing or sniffing that much," he said.
Faldo was the only big name in the field to make a move on a day when Greg Norman (73), Tom Lehman (73) and Nick Price (72) all went backwards, falling eight strokes off the pace.
"I'm new to this course. I'm having to grind hard," said Faldo. "I'm trying to hit as many solid shots as possible, and the putter is working better, so that's a nice feeling."
Faldo would love a victory as a confidence booster for next week's major.
But he is happy simply to be playing well going into the tournament he would most love to add to his three British Opens and three Masters titles.
